content.comment_body: I'm attempting to transfer a program from my computer to a [product_name] ([article_no]). Each time I try to connect to the device using various methods in [product_name] software (via the Tools->Transfer menu, or through the Network Project tab), I can see the device entry after refreshing from the Transfer menu or by going online in the Network view. However, when I test the connection, it fails and reports 'Unable to access the remote device.' I have tried connecting from two different PCs, both directly wired to the device and through a router. In every setup, I am able to ping the device and the device can ping my PC, but the connection test does not succeed. I also disabled the Windows Firewall but it made no difference. For reference, my original PC used IP 192.168.0.118 while the device was set to 192.168.0.15. Subnet mask is 255.255.255.0, gateway is 192.168.0.1. If needed, I could use Wireshark to investigate network packets, but I'm not sure what I should be looking for. I've reviewed several other related posts, but none seem relevant in my case.
Which [product_name] device are you using? Is it [article_no] Standard or FS04? Also, which [product_name] software version do you have?
The software I'm using is [product_name] [version_no] (2016-07-14 16-34). The hardware is [article_no]. I assume this corresponds to a standard version, not FS.
I found a 2D barcode on the device with FS-04 indicated below it, so it appears I have the FS-04 model.

Have you selected FS.04 in the device selection menu? There's an 'i' icon at the bottom right. If the software identifies an error, the icon will animate. Clicking it provides error details. Could you share a screenshot of this information?

I've attached a screenshot—though it doesn’t seem to provide much detail. As a side note, after using Wireshark yesterday, I observed significant traffic during connection attempts. I noticed that the device served a login page, so I tried accessing it via a browser and successfully saw the login page, but when trying to log in, I received a message saying the Web Server was disabled, which isn't unexpected. There is clear communication occurring, but the [product_name] software does not accept the connection.
Just to clarify, yes—I did set the device type to FS04, which appears in the lower right corner next to the info icon.

This might seem obvious, but is the [product_name] version included in the [product_name] Starter Kits the full version, or is it limited like the downloadable Demo Version? My behavior matches what you described—everything works except downloading. However, I would have expected a limited version to indicate restricted features, with greyed-out options or a notice about disabled functionality. I also wouldn’t expect the device and software to perform extensive Ethernet communications only for a connection test to fail. I'm running out of ideas.

analysis.insight_summary: The user consistently encounters failures when attempting to download programs from their PC to a [product_name] ([article_no], FS04 model) using [product_name] [version_no]. While the device can be discovered and successful pings confirm network connectivity, the software fails on the connection test with an 'Unable to access the remote device' error. The user verifies correct device selection, tries multiple computers and network configurations, disables the firewall, and inspects traffic with Wireshark. Despite visible network activity, the software provides limited diagnostic feedback, leaving the user questioning whether licensing or version restrictions may be contributing to the connectivity problem.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects dependable, straightforward connectivity between [product_name] software and the hardware device, along with clear, actionable feedback should connection issues arise. Additionally, the user seeks transparency regarding software licensing and any functional limitations.
